memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When the news reached Pharaoh's palace that Joseph's brothers had come, Pharaoh and all his officials were pleased. Pharaoh said to Joseph, 'Tell your brothers, "Do this: Load your animals and return to the land of Canaan, and bring your father and your families back to me. I will give you the best of the land of Egypt and you can enjoy the fat of the land."'" — Gen 45:16-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Something worth noticing: Pharaoh is genuinely glad. He does not merely tolerate Joseph's family arriving; he is pleased, and he offers them the best of Egypt.

Why? Because of Joseph. Pharaoh has never met these men. He knows nothing of their character. But he knows Joseph, and Joseph's standing is enough to secure a welcome for his whole family.

That is a picture worth holding onto. We are not welcomed by God on the strength of our own record. We come in on the standing of Another. God accepts us because of who Christ is and what He has done, and we are told we are accepted "in the Beloved" (Eph 1:6). Our welcome rests on His worth, not on ours.

The brothers had nothing to offer Egypt. They were shepherds from a famine-struck land with empty sacks and a guilty history. And they were offered the best of everything, because of their brother.

If you ever wonder whether God is glad to have you, remember what your welcome is built on. It is not your performance this week. It is Christ, and He has not changed.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you try to earn a welcome from God, or rest in Christ's standing?
2. How does it feel to know God is genuinely pleased to receive you in Christ?
3. Who has benefited in your life because of someone else's favour?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I come to You not on my own record but on Christ's. Thank You that I am accepted in the Beloved and that Your welcome does not depend on my performance. Amen.
